project.name: loopr-v5
project.description: Agent orchestrator with Plan decomposition as a central feature; a clean-break Rust workspace rewrite from v4 organized as a compiler-style pipeline of typed stages, each in its own crate. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: cli.rs
nodes.summary: Clap-derive CLI definition for the loopr binary, declaring the top-level Cli struct, the Command enum (Init/Plan/Plans/Works/Bundles/Ticks/Show/Daemon/Logs/Sessions/Director/Tui), and per-verb subcommand enums.

nodes.name: Cli
nodes.summary: Top-level clap parser struct holding global flags (chdir, log-level, output, session) and the Command subcommand selector.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Top-level subcommand enum mirroring stage boundaries: Init, Plan, Plans, Works, Bundles, Ticks, Show, Daemon, Logs, Sessions, Director, Tui.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Returns a stable short label for each Command variant; used for telemetry span names and log fields.

nodes.name: PlanCmd
nodes.summary: Subcommand enum for the plan verb: Create (start a Plan from a goal) and Override (force a Plan into a different status).

nodes.name: DirectorCmd
nodes.summary: Subcommand enum for the director verb: Chat (post operator note) and Status (read live Director snapshot).

nodes.name: LogsCmd
nodes.summary: Subcommand enum for the logs verb: Tail (follow latest run) and Runs (list previous runs).

nodes.name: SessionsCmd
nodes.summary: Subcommand enum for sessions verb: List, New, Resume, End, Status; manipulates the .loopr/active-session pointer.

nodes.name: DaemonCmd
nodes.summary: Subcommand enum for the daemon verb: Start (with --foreground), Stop, Status.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Clap parsing tests covering every Command variant, global flag (chdir, log-level, output), and the Command::label coverage exhaustiveness check.

nodes.name: commands.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel that re-exports the five subcommand handler modules (director, init, list, sessions, show).

nodes.name: director.rs
nodes.summary: Client-side handlers for `loopr director chat` and `loopr director status`; opens a tokio runtime, dispatches DirectorChat / DirectorStatus IPC methods, and pretty-prints the operator status snapshot.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry-point dispatcher for director subcommands; builds a tokio runtime and routes to chat or status.

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: Connects to the daemon, sends an operator note to the per-Plan NotesStore via the director.chat IPC method, and prints the assigned note id.

nodes.name: status
nodes.summary: Reads the live DirectorStatusSnapshot for a Plan via the director.status IPC method and renders it for the operator.

nodes.name: print_status
nodes.summary: Pretty-prints a DirectorStatusSnapshot showing mode, streaks, last action, unread notes, and needs-operator iteration count.

nodes.name: init.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `loopr init`: idempotent per-target setup that creates .loopr/, opens TaskStore, installs git hooks, appends to .git/info/exclude, and seeds baked prompt templates onto disk.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Top-level init entry point running every per-target setup step in sequence and aggregating their StepOutcomes into an InitOutcome report.

nodes.name: step_verify_source_guard
nodes.summary: Refuses to init when the target lives inside the loopr source tree; loopr never targets itself.

nodes.name: step_create_loopr_dir
nodes.summary: Creates the .loopr directory under the target if absent; reports Created vs Preserved.

nodes.name: step_open_taskstore
nodes.summary: Opens (or creates) the TaskStore for the target, ensuring JSONL + SQLite indexes are initialized.

nodes.name: step_install_taskstore_hooks
nodes.summary: Installs the taskstore git hooks (post-commit / post-merge) into the target repo so out-of-band edits stay in sync with the store.

nodes.name: step_ensure_git_excludes
nodes.summary: Appends loopr-specific patterns to .git/info/exclude so transcripts, summaries, and worktrees don't leak into commits.

nodes.name: step_seed_prompts
nodes.summary: Copies the baked-in prompt templates into the target's .loopr/prompts/ tree, preserving operator edits unless --force is given.

nodes.name: seed_prompts
nodes.summary: Public seeding entry point; walks the baked prompt manifest and dispatches to seed_dir for each top-level directory.

nodes.name: seed_dir
nodes.summary: Recursively copies a baked prompt directory tree to the destination, skipping .gitkeep files and respecting the merge/force policy.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for prompt seeding (empty target, gitkeep handling, preserve vs force merge) and end-to-end init.run idempotence on fresh and already-initialized targets.

nodes.name: list.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the `plans` / `works` / `bundles` / `ticks` list verbs by calling the record.list IPC method, validating the response kind matches the request, and rendering as JSON/YAML/text.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for the list verbs; builds a tokio runtime, dispatches record.list over IPC, validates kind, resolves output format, and renders the result.

nodes.name: validate_kind_match
nodes.summary: Asserts the RecordsResult kind returned by the daemon matches the kind the CLI requested; returns ClientIo error on mismatch.

nodes.name: sessions.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `loopr sessions` verbs (list, new, resume, end, status) directly against the session manifest store and the .loopr/active-session pointer; runs without contacting the daemon.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches sessions verbs to their handler functions.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Lists every persisted session manifest, marking the currently-active session.

nodes.name: end
nodes.summary: Closes the active session: aggregates per-process digests into a session summary.md and clears the .loopr/active-session pointer.

nodes.name: status
nodes.summary: Prints the active session's id, start time, and per-process digest paths.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Integration tests for the sessions verbs covering list / new / resume / end / status against a temporary XDG-style fixture.

nodes.name: show.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `loopr show <record-id>`: routes the id to its record kind by ID prefix, fetches via record.get IPC, and renders in the chosen format.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for show: determines record kind from id prefix, dispatches record.get over IPC, and renders the result.

nodes.name: kind_from_prefix
nodes.summary: Resolves a record id's type-prefix (p-/w-/b-/t-) to its RecordKind enum, returning UnknownIdPrefix on unrecognized inputs.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for kind_from_prefix covering every current record-id prefix, unknown prefixes, missing dashes, empty strings, and truncated ids.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: Top-level loopr Config (llm, tools, worktree, agents, integrator, transport sections); loads from .loopr/config.yml with LOOPR_CONFIG env override and exposes resolve_api_key for the LLM section.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Root configuration struct composing every stage's config section (llm, tools, worktree, agents, integrator, transport).

nodes.name: IntegratorSection
nodes.summary: Integrator-specific config (validation_commands, validation_timeout_secs) with into_integrator_config conversion to the integrator crate's typed config.

nodes.name: TransportSection
nodes.summary: Transport timeouts: client_request_secs, server_idle_secs, server_write_secs, daemon_startup_secs; bounds every IPC and daemon-startup wait.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads the Config from <target>/.loopr/config.yml, falling back to default if absent and applying the LOOPR_CONFIG env override on top.

nodes.name: resolve_api_key
nodes.summary: Reads the LLM API key from the env var named by llm.api_key_env, falling back to a placeholder if unset (for offline tests).

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Config tests covering missing-file default, llm/tools/worktree section parsing, unknown-field rejection, env overrides, transport defaults, and resolve_api_key fallback behavior.

nodes.name: daemon.rs
nodes.summary: Daemon process lifecycle: double-fork detachment, pid/version/process-id sentinels, signal handling, accept-loop bootstrap, and reverse-toposort drain (implementer to reviewer to director to work-spawner to integrator) on shutdown.

nodes.name: drain_implementer_tasks
nodes.summary: Drains the implementer JoinSet at shutdown with a soft timeout, then abort_all + drain the residue.

nodes.name: drain_reviewer_tasks
nodes.summary: Drains the reviewer JoinSet at shutdown with a soft timeout, then abort_all + drain the residue.

nodes.name: drain_integrator_tasks
nodes.summary: Drains the integrator JoinSet at shutdown, the terminal pool in the reverse-toposort drain order.

nodes.name: drain_director_tasks
nodes.summary: Drains the director JoinSet (Opus LLM calls) at shutdown with a soft timeout matching the streaming window.

nodes.name: drain_work_spawner_tasks
nodes.summary: Drains the work-spawner JoinSet (Director-issued accept_bundle / override_work / assign_work tasks).

nodes.name: ensure_daemon
nodes.summary: Parent-side entry that double-forks into the daemon process if no live daemon is running for the target.

nodes.name: ensure_daemon_if_needed
nodes.summary: Conditionally starts a daemon for the target: skip when one is already alive on the matching version, otherwise call ensure_daemon.

nodes.name: run_grandchild
nodes.summary: Grandchild-side code path: never returns; calls daemon_main and process::exit so unwinding cannot hit the parent's telemetry init.

nodes.name: daemon_main
nodes.summary: Daemon top-level entry: writes pid/version/process-id sentinels, builds a tokio runtime, and invokes run_active_daemon.

nodes.name: run_active_daemon
nodes.summary: Active daemon body: builds context, calls serve_core, drains task pools in reverse-toposort order, writes the run digest, and exits cleanly.

nodes.name: bound_startup
nodes.summary: Wraps a future with the configured daemon-startup wall-clock cap, returning LooprError::DaemonStartup on elapsed.

nodes.name: build_context
nodes.summary: Builds the DaemonContext: opens TaskStore, applies worktree reconcile sweep, wires LLM client + lane router + sandbox + every agent config from .loopr/config.yml.

nodes.name: serve_core
nodes.summary: Inner serve loop: spawns the signal watcher and the IPC accept loop, then awaits shutdown_notify before returning to run_active_daemon for drain.

nodes.name: write_process_digest_best_effort
nodes.summary: Writes runs/<pid>/summary.md from the accumulated ProcessSnapshot on graceful exit; logs a warn! on failure and returns.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Public serve entry point used by run_active_daemon; binds the unix socket, runs the accept loop, and coordinates shutdown with serve_core.

nodes.name: spawn_signal_watcher
nodes.summary: Spawns a tokio task that watches SIGTERM/SIGINT and calls shutdown_notify to begin graceful drain.

nodes.name: context.rs
nodes.summary: The DaemonContext: shared per-daemon state holding store, summary fanout, every agent JoinSet, work/bundle scope maps, and the per-Plan operator_notifies / director_statuses sidecars; also hosts the spawn_* methods for implementer/reviewer/integrator and the transition_and_persist_* FSM-with-persist helpers.

nodes.name: DaemonContext
nodes.summary: Central daemon state container: target, session/process ids, store, summary fanout, llm + router + sandbox, per-role JoinSets, scope id maps, per-Plan operator_notifies, director_statuses, snapshot, and server timeouts.

nodes.name: ScopedIdGuard
nodes.summary: RAII guard that inserts an id into a shared map on construction and removes it on Drop (panic-safe via unwind cleanup).

nodes.name: PlanSummaryExtras
nodes.summary: Extras passed to transition_and_persist_plan: per-Plan tick count, bundles accepted, bundles rejected.

nodes.name: spawn_implementer_for_work
nodes.summary: Spawns an Implementer task for a Work record: ensures worktree, builds deps, runs the agents::implementer ralph loop, and persists the resulting bundle via the SummaryFanout sink.

nodes.name: spawn_reviewer_for_bundle
nodes.summary: Spawns a Reviewer task for a Bundle: builds review prompt, calls the LLM, parses the verdict, and either accepts or rejects the bundle.

nodes.name: spawn_integrator_for_bundle
nodes.summary: Spawns an Integrator task for an accepted Bundle: merges the per-Plan integration branch, runs validation_commands, and persists the bundle outcome.

nodes.name: promote_unblocked_siblings
nodes.summary: Reactive-execution helper: when a Work terminates, transitions every sibling whose deps are all done from Pending to Ready and dispatches an implementer for it.

nodes.name: block_dependent_siblings
nodes.summary: Reactive-execution helper: when a Work fails, transitions every dependent Work to Blocked with a reason pointing at the terminal work id.

nodes.name: transition_and_persist_work
nodes.summary: FSM-with-persist helper: validates the proposed Work transition against the Fsm-derived table, bumps attempt_count on Ready, enforces the MAX_WORK_ATTEMPTS_HARD_CAP, and writes through the summary fanout.

nodes.name: transition_and_persist_plan
nodes.summary: FSM-with-persist helper for Plans: validates the proposed Plan transition, emits the terminal-state info! summary line on terminal transitions, and writes through the summary fanout.

nodes.name: spawner.rs
nodes.summary: DaemonSpawner: the Director-facing facade implementing the agents::WorkSpawner trait. Hosts accept_bundle / override_work / assign_work / spawn_reviewer / spawn_integrator entry points and recover_in_progress_work for crash recovery.

nodes.name: DaemonSpawner
nodes.summary: Thin Arc<DaemonContext> wrapper implementing the agents::WorkSpawner trait so Director-issued spawn requests cross into daemon-owned JoinSets.

nodes.name: accept_bundle
nodes.summary: Director-issued accept_bundle: transitions the bundle to Accepted, spawns an integrator task into integrator_tasks, tracked under work_spawner_tasks.

nodes.name: override_work
nodes.summary: Director-issued Work override: transitions the work to a Director-chosen status with a reason; spawns a fresh Implementer when target_status is Ready.

nodes.name: assign_work
nodes.summary: Director-issued assign_work: re-checks dependency readiness and spawns an Implementer task for a Work that the reactive layer hasn't already dispatched.

nodes.name: spawn_reviewer
nodes.summary: Spawns a reviewer task into reviewer_tasks for the given bundle, tracking the bundle id under reviewer_bundle_ids.

nodes.name: spawn_integrator
nodes.summary: Spawns an integrator task into integrator_tasks for the given accepted bundle, tracking the bundle id under integrator_bundle_ids.

nodes.name: recover_in_progress_work
nodes.summary: Crash-recovery helper: transitions a Work stuck InProgress back to Ready with a reason so the next implementer spawn can pick it up.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for ScopedIdGuard: insert-on-construction, remove-on-drop, panic-unwind cleanup, and independent-key invariants under concurrent guards.

nodes.name: fork.rs
nodes.summary: libc-level double-fork primitive that detaches the daemon from the controlling terminal; redirects stdio to /dev/null and reports ForkOutcome::Parent vs Daemon.

nodes.name: double_fork
nodes.summary: Classic double-fork detach: fork, setsid in child, fork again, parent waitpid + exit, grandchild becomes the daemon with stdio redirected to /dev/null.

nodes.name: redirect_stdio_to_devnull
nodes.summary: Opens /dev/null and dup2s it onto stdin/stdout/stderr so the daemon has no terminal handles.

nodes.name: last_errno
nodes.summary: Reads errno via *libc::__errno_location() / *libc::__error() and returns it as an io::Error.

nodes.name: git.rs
nodes.summary: Daemon-side git helper that ensures the per-Plan integration branch exists (idempotent), creating it from HEAD when missing.

nodes.name: ensure_integration_branch
nodes.summary: Verifies the loopr/<plan-id> integration branch exists in the target repo, creating it from HEAD if not; idempotent on repeated calls.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for ensure_integration_branch: create-from-HEAD, idempotent second call, and the fresh-repo-without-HEAD error path.

nodes.name: handle.rs
nodes.summary: DaemonHandle: a small public façade over a subset of DaemonContext (shutting_down, shutdown_notify, socket_path) that the transport layer holds without keeping the full context alive.

nodes.name: DaemonHandle
nodes.summary: Thin façade exposing shutdown signaling and the unix socket path; cloned via Arc fields without prolonging DaemonContext.

nodes.name: sentinel.rs
nodes.summary: Filesystem sentinels in .loopr/: pid, version, process-id, and unix socket path helpers, plus is_daemon_alive / process_name_is_loopr / kill_stale routines that reconcile stale daemon files.

nodes.name: write_pid
nodes.summary: Writes the daemon pid file using create_new so a concurrent daemon write fails fast rather than racing.

nodes.name: read_pid
nodes.summary: Reads the pid file (returns Ok(None) if missing) and parses it as a u32.

nodes.name: is_daemon_alive
nodes.summary: Checks whether the recorded pid is still alive (kill 0) AND the process name is loopr, to avoid mistaking a reused pid for our daemon.

nodes.name: process_name_is_loopr
nodes.summary: Reads /proc/<pid>/comm (Linux) or invokes ps -p (other unix) to confirm the recorded pid is actually our daemon binary.

nodes.name: kill_stale
nodes.summary: Reconciles a stale daemon: sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after a grace) and cleans up pid/socket files.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Removes pid, version, process-id, and socket files from .loopr/ when the daemon exits gracefully.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for pid file write/read round-trip, exclusive-create collisions, version matching, and clean() behavior in a tempdir.

nodes.name: startup.rs
nodes.summary: Daemon-startup reconcile: sweeps stale worktrees, requeues unfinished reviewer/integrator bundles, promotes dep-ready siblings, and re-spawns Directors for live Plans (startup_reconcile_directors).

nodes.name: ReconcileReport
nodes.summary: Counts the reconcile pass observed: cleaned worktrees, orphans, carried-forward records, foreign skips, requeued reviewers/integrators, terminal bundles, and corruption hits.

nodes.name: reconcile
nodes.summary: Top-level startup reconcile entry: sweeps worktrees, sweeps bundles, promotes deps, and re-spawns Directors; returns the ReconcileReport for digest emission.

nodes.name: sweep_worktrees
nodes.summary: Lists every worktree under .loopr/worktrees/, matches it against its work id, and cleans up worktree + branch when the work is terminal.

nodes.name: sweep_bundles
nodes.summary: Walks every non-terminal Bundle and respawns either a reviewer (PendingReview) or an integrator (Accepted) so an in-flight pipeline survives a daemon restart.

nodes.name: sweep_dep_promotions
nodes.summary: For every Active Plan, runs promote_unblocked_siblings to dispatch any Work whose deps became ready while the daemon was down.

nodes.name: startup_reconcile_directors
nodes.summary: For every Active Plan, recreates its operator_notifies entry and respawns the Director task so cross-restart operator chat and stuck-state recovery resume cleanly.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for the startup-reconcile sweeps covering worktree cleanup, bundle requeue, and dep-promotion against fixture stores.

nodes.name: summary_fanout.rs
nodes.summary: SummaryFanout<S>: decorator that implements WorkUpdateSink / BundleUpdateSink / PlanUpdateSink by writing through the inner sink and then re-rendering the matching summary.md; Work updates also refresh the parent Plan summary.

nodes.name: SummaryFanout
nodes.summary: Generic decorator wrapping an inner sink with summary-write side effects; parameterized over the underlying sink type so it can layer over the real store or a fake.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for SummaryFanout covering write-through + summary.md emission for each record kind and the parent-Plan refresh on Work updates.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for bound_startup: pass-through-ok, inner-error propagation, and the elapsed -> DaemonStartup error path.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: LooprError: typed thiserror enum covering source-guard trips, target validation, telemetry init, session resolve, client I/O, daemon startup, lock loss, handshake, RPC, unknown id prefix, TUI absence, and corruption gate.

nodes.name: LooprError
nodes.summary: Typed thiserror enum: every variant carries the structured context (path, expected version, breach duration, error code) callers need to handle the failure.

nodes.name: guard.rs
nodes.summary: Source guard: refuses to operate when the target path lives inside the loopr source tree (sentinel file detected via ancestor walk), enforcing 'loopr is never the target'.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Walks ancestors of `start`; if any contains the .loopr-source-guard sentinel, returns SourceGuardTripped so the run aborts before mutating the loopr repo itself.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the source-guard module that prevents loopr from being run against its own source repository.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Library entry point for the loopr binary crate; runs the CLI, dispatches subcommands across daemon/plan/session/logs modules, and resolves tracing log directives.
nodes.languageNotes: Thin lib.rs / thick CLI pattern: the binary's main.rs forwards to lib::run, which fans out to module-level dispatch functions.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Top-level CLI entry point invoked by main.rs; initializes telemetry, resolves the effective target, and dispatches to per-subcommand handlers.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Routes a parsed command to the appropriate handler with session/process/format context after the daemon connection is established.

nodes.name: daemon_status
nodes.summary: Implements the loopr daemon status subcommand by querying the live daemon via IPC and rendering its lifecycle state.

nodes.name: plan_create_command
nodes.summary: Client-side body for loopr plan create: builds the IPC request payload, connects to the daemon, and prints the resulting plan id.

nodes.name: plan_override_command
nodes.summary: Client-side body for loopr plan override: sends a status-override IPC request for a given plan id.

nodes.name: daemon_stop
nodes.summary: Stops the running daemon for a target by sending an IPC shutdown request, falling back to a no-op when no daemon is bound.

nodes.name: logs.rs
nodes.summary: Thin module exposing log-related helpers (e.g., directory resolution and tail) used by the loopr logs subcommand.

nodes.name: main.rs
nodes.summary: Binary entry point: parses CLI args with clap and delegates to lib::run, keeping main.rs intentionally thin.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the project-wide thin-main, thick-lib convention so the library is independently testable.

nodes.name: output.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Format enum (Text/Json/Yaml/Auto) and render helper that serializes any serializable value into the operator-requested output format.

nodes.name: Format
nodes.summary: Enum of supported output formats; resolves Auto against stdout TTY state to pick a default.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering Format::resolve auto-detection and the render helper for each output format.

nodes.name: session.rs
nodes.summary: Owns the SessionId lifecycle: resolves the active session from CLI/pointer/fresh-allocation, manages the .loopr/active-session pointer with exclusive-claim semantics, and backs the loopr sessions verb family.
nodes.languageNotes: Pointer file is claimed under an exclusive lock to prevent two daemons racing for the same session.

nodes.name: resolve_session_id
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective SessionId for the current process from --session flag, the .loopr/active-session pointer, or by allocating a fresh one.

nodes.name: claim_pointer_exclusive
nodes.summary: Acquires an exclusive lock on the active-session pointer file before mutating its contents to prevent concurrent daemons from racing for ownership.

nodes.name: attach_pointer
nodes.summary: Writes the resolved SessionId into the .loopr/active-session pointer with claim semantics and atomic-rename safety.

nodes.name: end_active
nodes.summary: Implements loopr sessions end by clearing the active-session pointer and rolling the session manifest into its terminal form.

nodes.name: list_all
nodes.summary: Implements loopr sessions list by reading XDG-backed session manifest directories and returning chronological entries.

nodes.name: session_processes
nodes.summary: Enumerates every process recorded under a given session manifest, reading per-process metadata and exit status.

nodes.name: read_pointer_state
nodes.summary: Reads the .loopr/active-session pointer and decodes its current PointerState (vacant, claimed, or detached).

nodes.name: allocate_new_session
nodes.summary: Allocates a fresh SessionId, creates its XDG manifest directory, and writes the initial SessionManifest.

nodes.name: SessionManifest
nodes.summary: Serializable manifest record describing a session's identity, creation time, and lifecycle state.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering session pointer resolution, exclusive-claim semantics, and the loopr sessions verb bodies.

nodes.name: bundle.rs
nodes.summary: Renders per-Bundle markdown digest at .loopr/records/bundles/<id>/summary.md; pure render + atomic write helpers.

nodes.name: render_bundle
nodes.summary: Produces the bundle summary markdown body from a Bundle record, including status, work refs, and review status.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Summary-module root: exposes per-record renderers (bundle, plan, work) and the shared atomic_write helper used by every summary writer.

nodes.name: plan.rs
nodes.summary: Renders per-Plan markdown digest including child Work rollups at .loopr/records/plans/<id>/summary.md.

nodes.name: render_plan
nodes.summary: Produces the Plan markdown body, embedding per-child Work statuses so operators see the rollup without traversing records.

nodes.name: work.rs
nodes.summary: Renders per-Work markdown digest at .loopr/records/works/<id>/summary.md; written after every Work FSM transition.

nodes.name: render_work
nodes.summary: Produces the Work summary markdown body covering status, acceptance criteria, attempt count, and lifecycle annotations.

nodes.name: target.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective project target directory by preferring the explicit -C chdir flag, then walking up for a .git toplevel or .loopr marker.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves the target directory for a loopr invocation from CLI/env/CWD with precedence rules baked in.

nodes.name: git_toplevel
nodes.summary: Walks upward from a starting path to find the nearest git working-tree root, returning None if none is found.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Library-level unit tests covering cross-module helpers including target resolution, log directive parsing, and CLI plumbing.

nodes.name: transport.rs
nodes.summary: Transport module root: defines ClientTimeouts and ServerTimeouts (config-derived budgets) and the connect_or_wait helper that opens an IpcClient with retry semantics.

nodes.name: ClientTimeouts
nodes.summary: Bundles operator-tunable client-side IPC timeouts derived from TransportSection config.

nodes.name: ServerTimeouts
nodes.summary: Bundles server-side IPC timeouts (idle, write, startup budgets) used by the daemon's accept loop.

nodes.name: connect_or_wait_with_timeouts
nodes.summary: Opens an IpcClient against the target socket, optionally spawning the daemon if needed, with caller-supplied timeout budgets.

nodes.name: client.rs
nodes.summary: Client side of the IPC transport: opens a UnixStream against the daemon, performs handshake (carries session id and protocol version), and issues request/response RPC under a wall-clock cap.

nodes.name: IpcClient
nodes.summary: Connected IPC client holding the framed Unix stream and session-state required to issue typed RPC calls to the daemon.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens a UnixStream to the daemon socket and wraps it in the LinesCodec framed client with the configured 1 MiB max line.

nodes.name: handshake
nodes.summary: Performs the IPC handshake by sending the client's session_id and protocol version and asserting the daemon's match.

nodes.name: request_impl
nodes.summary: Inner RPC engine that frames a request, awaits the matching response under a wall-clock cap, and maps timeouts to LooprError::ClientIo with the breached duration.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering IpcClient framing, handshake error paths, request/response correlation, and timeout enforcement against a stub server.

nodes.name: handler.rs
nodes.summary: Server-side IPC dispatch: maps each Method to its handler (plan create, record list/get, director chat, plan override, director status), enforces handshake state, and uniformly maps store errors back to wire responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Every handler is #[tracing::instrument] so its span inherits the request_id and client_session_id from the connection span.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Top-level request router that enforces the handshake state and routes each Method variant to its handler with the DaemonContext.

nodes.name: handle_handshake
nodes.summary: Validates the client's protocol version and session_id, transitions the connection from Unhandshaken to Active, and emits the handshake response.

nodes.name: handle_plan_create
nodes.summary: Implements the plan.create IPC verb: persists a Plan record from the operator goal, starts a Director task with a wake-up Notify, and returns the new plan id.

nodes.name: handle_record_get

nodes.name: Input

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Edit output: resolved path, bytes written, and number of replacements (always 1 on success).

nodes.name: execute

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Glob input: a single pattern string that is rejected when absolute under sandbox.

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Glob output: list of canonicalized matching paths inside the working directory.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Compile the glob pattern, reject absolute paths under sandbox, walk matches, and filter results to those that canonicalize inside the working dir.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Grep input carrying pattern, optional path, case-insensitivity flag, and optional output cap.

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Grep output carrying match lines, the match count, and a truncated flag set when the cap was hit.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Read input: target path with optional offset and limit for pagination (default 500 lines).

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Read output carrying line-numbered content, lines shown, total lines, and a truncation flag.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Write input: target path and content string to create or overwrite.

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Write output: resolved path, bytes written, and a created-vs-overwrote flag.

nodes.name: ToolsConfig
nodes.summary: Kebab-cased serde struct that the loopr binary composes into its top-level Config — fields: sandbox, path_deny_patterns, bash_denylist_extend.

nodes.name: DenyEntryConfig
nodes.summary: Config entry for a single bash-denylist extension: a token sequence and a human-readable reason.

nodes.name: BashDenylist
nodes.summary: Holds the active deny patterns and walks a parsed bash tree to detect any matching token subsequence, returning the offending pattern's reason.

nodes.name: DenyPattern
nodes.summary: A single denylist rule — a sequence of token matchers and the reason string surfaced to operators on rejection.

nodes.name: ToolError

nodes.name: Lane
nodes.summary: Tri-state enum (Local/Net/Heavy) plus an as_str helper returning the lowercase string used in tracing span fields.

nodes.name: LanePolicy
nodes.summary: Const policy table per lane carrying slot cap, default and max timeouts, and a sandbox-net flag — Local: 10 slots, Net: 5, Heavy: 1.

nodes.name: LaneRouter
nodes.summary: Per-lane tokio semaphore pool that acquires a slot before spawning, applies env scrubbing and bwrap wrapping when warranted, and propagates timeouts back to the caller.

nodes.name: RouterInitError

nodes.name: SandboxMode
nodes.summary: Tri-state sandbox posture (Required/Preferred/Off) serialized as lowercase YAML; default is Required.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the bwrap sandbox module covering SandboxMode serde, the bwrap functional probe, and the bwrap_command wrapper that re-emits sh -c invocations through bubblewrap.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering schema_value generation against a Dummy input struct to lock in field naming and object shape.

nodes.name: shell.rs
nodes.summary: Tiny helper that builds a configured tokio::process::Command for `sh -c <script>` with piped stdio and an explicit working directory; reused by sandbox and tool implementations.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Single unit test that snapshots the argv shape of sh_command to guard against accidental flag drift.

nodes.name: spawn.rs

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Integration-style unit tests for spawn_with_process_group covering exit-code propagation, timeout enforcement, combined-output capture, and persisted-output sidecar files.

nodes.name: tool.rs
nodes.summary: Core Tool trait that every builtin tool implements (name/description/lane/schema/execute) and the ToolContext struct carrying the working directory, router, sandbox config, and denylists into each invocation.

nodes.name: dispatch.rs
nodes.summary: Integration tests for tool dispatch (sandbox routing, denylist enforcement, lane classification) exercised end-to-end against a real router + sandbox + denylist composition.

nodes.name: instrumentation.rs
nodes.summary: Visibility contract tests that parse the production events.log shape and assert tool spans carry the required telemetry fields (lane, tool, action_kind).

nodes.name: tool_visibility.rs
nodes.summary: Tests verifying tool-level visibility events (router routing decisions, sandbox mode resolution) are emitted with the agreed field shape for operator grep cookbooks.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Per-crate scope rules for the tools crate, defining what belongs here (Tool trait, builtins, lane classification, bwrap sandbox) versus what stays in agents (orchestration) or domain (records).

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Cargo manifest for the tools crate declaring its dependency surface (domain, telemetry, tokio, schemars, serde) and workspace-inherited version.

nodes.name: .otto.yml
nodes.summary: Scoped otto CI configuration for the tools crate covering lint, check, test, and whitespace passes run by `otto ci` inside this crate directory.

nodes.name: action.rs
nodes.summary: AgentAction enum: the canonical set of actions an implementer agent can emit (RunTool, CommitChanges, ProposeBundle, Done, NeedHelp) plus a kind() helper used by the lifeguard and dispatcher.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: Per-role config structs (ImplementerConfig, ReviewerConfig, DirectorConfig) and their composed AgentsConfig, with serde-kebab-case defaults that the daemon reads from YAML.

nodes.name: director.rs

nodes.name: mode.rs

nodes.summary: Unit tests asserting every DirectorMode transition: Normal->Conservative on repeat/no-progress, Conservative->NeedsOperator on escalation, recovery paths, and operator-note overrides.

nodes.summary: DirectorPatternTracker: ring-buffered history of action fingerprints and state hashes that detects same-action loops, no-progress streaks, and escalation thresholds to drive Director mode transitions.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Comprehensive unit tests for DirectorPatternTracker covering window size, thresholds, fingerprint mutating vs read-only classification, and observation emission ordering.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Large suite of integration tests exercising run_director_inner against fake LLM/store/spawner: covers action parsing, restart reasons, reconcile recovery, NeedsOperator grace, and full mode-transition flows.

nodes.name: operator.rs
nodes.summary: Director tests focused on the operator-intervention path: note delivery, NeedsOperator grace counter, Stalled escalation, and mode reset on operator-note arrival.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit and integration tests for dispatch_action and propose_bundle covering tool routing, scope-file commits, partial-commit-for-inspection, and patch-id computation against a real temp worktree.

nodes.name: implementer.rs

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for run_implementer covering iteration cap, lifeguard escalation, parse-failure budget, bundle persistence, and force_propose fallback when the LLM produces no actionable response.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root that wires the per-role modules (action, config, director, dispatch, implementer, lifeguard, parse, reviewer, scope) and re-exports the public agent API used by loopr.

nodes.name: lifeguard.rs
nodes.summary: Lifeguard guardrail used by every Ralph loop: canonicalises an AgentAction to an FNV hash, counts repeats, tracks consecutive parse failures, and returns Decision::Continue or Decision::Escalate when thresholds trip.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering Lifeguard::check_action repeat counting, canonical_hash stability across key reordering, and record_parse_failure escalation thresholds.

nodes.name: spawn_with_process_group
nodes.summary: Spawns a child in its own setsid process group, captures stdout/stderr concurrently into bounded buffers, enforces timeout via kill strategy, and optionally persists the combined output to disk.

nodes.name: read_pipe_to_buffers
nodes.summary: Async pump that reads from a tokio child pipe and appends decoded chunks into target and combined-output buffers under a shared lock.

nodes.name: apply_kill
nodes.summary: Applies the requested KillStrategy when a child times out: SIGTERM the entire process group for Pgid, or kill only the bwrap parent for sandboxed BwrapChild children.

nodes.name: persist_combined
nodes.summary: Writes the combined stdout+stderr buffer to a synthesized filename under PersistConfig.base so callers can return a sidecar path instead of an oversized inline string.

nodes.name: KillStrategy
nodes.summary: Enum selecting how to terminate a timed-out child: Pgid (SIGTERM the whole process group) or BwrapChild (kill only the bubblewrap parent).

nodes.name: SpawnResult
nodes.summary: Result of spawn_with_process_group carrying stdout, stderr, combined output, exit code, duration, timeout flag, persisted path, and truncated flag.

nodes.name: PersistConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for sidecar output persistence: a base directory and a per-invocation id used to synthesize unique filenames.

nodes.name: Tool
nodes.summary: Core trait every builtin tool implements: name, description, lane (read vs mutating), JSON schema, and async execute(ctx, input).

nodes.name: ToolContext
nodes.summary: Per-invocation context carrying working_dir, router, sandbox config, path/bash denylists, persist base, and invocation_id into every Tool::execute call.

nodes.name: ToolSchema
nodes.summary: Wire-format schema record (name, description, input_schema) emitted to the LLM so it can fill in tool calls correctly.

nodes.name: for_tool
nodes.summary: Generic constructor that derives a ToolSchema from a Tool implementation, using schemars to produce the input_schema and pulling name/description from the trait.

nodes.name: sh_command
nodes.summary: Builds a tokio::process::Command for `sh -c <script>` with piped stdio and an explicit cwd; the shared shell-spawn primitive reused by sandbox and bash tools.

nodes.name: AgentAction
nodes.summary: Tagged enum of the actions an implementer agent can request: RunTool, CommitChanges, ProposeBundle, Done, NeedHelp. The canonical contract between LLM output and the dispatcher.

nodes.name: ImplementerConfig
nodes.summary: Implementer-loop tuning knobs: max_iterations, max_requeries, max_parse_failures, max_repeat_action, and force-propose caps for files and per-file size.

nodes.name: ReviewerConfig
nodes.summary: Reviewer-loop config: max_requeries, diff_byte_cap, and noop_files_byte_cap that bound how much of a bundle's diff is shown to the LLM reviewer.

nodes.name: DirectorConfig
nodes.summary: Director-loop config: poll intervals, restart and requery budgets, model, token_budget, max_work_attempts, reconcile_grace_secs, PatternConfig, and the NeedsOperator grace counter.

nodes.name: AgentsConfig
nodes.summary: Top-level agents config composed of ImplementerConfig, ReviewerConfig, and DirectorConfig; the YAML-deserialised entry point honoured by the daemon as of v0.7.11.

nodes.name: DirectorAction
nodes.summary: Tagged enum of the actions the Director LLM can emit: AcceptBundle, OverrideWork, AssignWork, Done, NeedHelp. Parsed from JSON in parse_director_actions.

nodes.name: DirectorError
nodes.summary: thiserror enum of recoverable and unrecoverable Director failures: Llm, Lifeguard, NeedHelp, Store, Parse, Context, Id, Fsm. Used by restart_reason_for to classify restart causes.

nodes.name: WorkSpawner
nodes.summary: Trait the Director uses to materialise its actions: accept_bundle, override_work, assign_work, spawn_reviewer, spawn_integrator, recover_in_progress_work, plus list_running_* helpers for reconciliation.

nodes.name: DirectorStore
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting the store reads the Director loop performs: list_works/list_bundles for a plan, get_work/get_plan, update_plan, list_unread_notes_for_plan, mark_notes_read.

nodes.name: DirectorStatusSnapshot
nodes.summary: Per-iteration snapshot written to DirectorDeps::director_statuses: mode, no_progress_streak, same_action_streak, iteration, last action kind/target/ts, unread_note_count, and Phase 10 needs_operator_iters.

nodes.name: DirectorDeps
nodes.summary: Generic dependency bundle for run_director: llm, store, context, spawner, config, shutdown signal, operator_notify channel, and the shared director_statuses RwLock map.

nodes.name: parse_director_actions
nodes.summary: Parses the LLM response as either a Vec<DirectorAction> or a single DirectorAction (object or array tolerance), emitting DirectorError::Parse with the underlying serde diagnostic.

nodes.name: build_director_state
nodes.summary: Loads the per-Plan state the LLM sees each iteration: works, bundles, plan, and unread notes; pulls them through the DirectorStore trait so tests can supply fakes.

nodes.name: reconcile_director
nodes.summary: Stuck-state recovery sweep run each iteration: looks for Triaged/Accepted bundles past the grace window and InProgress Work whose spawner is no longer running, then re-spawns reviewer/integrator or rolls the Work back to Ready.

nodes.name: run_director
nodes.summary: Outer Director loop entry point: instruments the span with plan_id, runs run_director_inner, and reports the restart reason on each restart up to DirectorConfig::max_restarts.

nodes.name: run_director_inner
nodes.summary: The Director loop body: builds state, calls the LLM, parses actions, applies them through the WorkSpawner, observes patterns, drives the DirectorMode FSM, handles NeedsOperator grace + Stalled escalation, and writes a DirectorStatusSnapshot per iteration.

nodes.name: director_accept_bundle
nodes.summary: Routing entry point invoked when the Director emits AcceptBundle; emits the Phase 7 routing info! event and delegates to spawner.accept_bundle.

nodes.name: restart_reason_for
nodes.summary: Closed-enum classifier mapping DirectorError to one of llm_retryable, parse_failure, context_failure, store_failure, id_failure, lifeguard_escalation, need_help for the restart_reason telemetry field.

nodes.name: fingerprint_for_action
nodes.summary: Maps a DirectorAction onto the ActionFingerprint shape the DirectorPatternTracker hashes for same-action detection.

nodes.name: DirectorMode
nodes.summary: Director mode FSM enum: Normal (default), Conservative (after a guardrail trip), NeedsOperator (after escalation). PascalCase as_str() feeds the mode telemetry field.

nodes.name: next_mode
nodes.summary: Pure transition function mapping (current_mode, PatternObservation) onto the next DirectorMode; the entire mode FSM lives in this match.

nodes.name: PatternConfig
nodes.summary: Tuning knobs for the DirectorPatternTracker: same_action_threshold, no_progress_threshold, escalation_threshold, and the ring-buffer window size.

nodes.name: ActionFingerprint
nodes.summary: Compact (kind, target_id, target_status) record the tracker hashes; carries constructors for accept_bundle/override_work/assign_work/done/need_help plus is_mutating().

nodes.name: PatternObservation
nodes.summary: Enum of observations the tracker emits each iteration: SameActionTripped, NoProgressTripped, EscalationTripped, Recovered, OperatorNoteArrived; consumed by next_mode.

nodes.name: DirectorPatternTracker
nodes.summary: Stateful tracker holding action_history, state_hash_history, no_progress_streak, and PatternConfig; emits PatternObservation values from observe() based on configured thresholds.

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Per-iteration observation pump: appends the new fingerprint and state hash to bounded windows, recomputes streaks, and returns the strongest PatternObservation that fires (same-action vs no-progress vs escalation vs recovered).

nodes.name: compute_state_hash
nodes.summary: Hashes the relevant fields of (works, bundles) into a stable u64 so the tracker can tell whether plan state moved between iterations.

nodes.name: ActionResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of dispatching one AgentAction: ToolOutput, Committed, NothingToCommit, BundleCreated, Done, NeedHelp, or Error. Drives the implementer loop's next-iteration decision.

nodes.name: DispatchError
nodes.summary: thiserror enum of dispatch failures: Git, Tool, Io. Wrapped by ImplementerError::Dispatch.

nodes.name: ToolExecutor
nodes.summary: Trait the dispatcher uses to invoke tools: async execute(tool_name, input, working_dir) returning the tool's textual output. RealTools implements it against the tools crate router.

nodes.name: RealTools
nodes.summary: Production ToolExecutor implementation wiring together the tools crate router, sandbox config, bash denylist, path-deny patterns, and persist-base directory.

nodes.name: dispatch_action
nodes.summary: Translates one AgentAction into an ActionResult by routing RunTool through the ToolExecutor, CommitChanges through commit_changes, ProposeBundle through propose_bundle, and surfacing Done/NeedHelp directly.

nodes.name: commit_changes
nodes.summary: Stages the provided scope_files in the worktree and commits them with the supplied message; returns NothingToCommit when staging is empty.

nodes.name: propose_bundle
nodes.summary: Builds a Bundle from the worktree: computes the name-status manifest against the base sha, derives patch_id and LOC-changed, and emits the canonical 'implementer produced bundle' info! event.

nodes.name: git_patch_id
nodes.summary: Computes a stable patch-id for a commit (or worktree diff) using `git patch-id`, with an oversize cap that falls back to a hash-of-name-status sentinel when the diff is too large.

nodes.name: ImplementerError
nodes.summary: thiserror enum of implementer-loop failures: EscalationNeeded, Llm, Sink, Context, Dispatch, Io. EscalationNeeded is the lifeguard-triggered exit.

nodes.name: BundleSink
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting bundle persistence so the implementer can write proposed bundles through the store without taking a direct store dependency.

nodes.name: Deps
nodes.summary: Implementer dependency bundle: llm, tools, bundles sink, context builder, ImplementerConfig, tool_schemas snapshot, and the per-run state used for transcript writing.

nodes.name: run_implementer
nodes.summary: The Implementer Ralph loop: each iteration assembles messages, queries the LLM, parses AgentActions, runs the lifeguard, dispatches each action, writes a transcript, and exits on Done/NeedHelp/escalation/bundle-produced.

nodes.name: force_propose
nodes.summary: Fallback path used when the LLM never emits ProposeBundle but the worktree has stageable changes: synthesises a bundle from modified tracked files (subject to max_force_propose_files and per-file size caps).

nodes.name: write_implementer_transcript
nodes.summary: Appends one iteration's transcript (system/user prompts, raw response, parsed actions, dispatcher outcomes, lifeguard decision) to the implementer transcript file for the work id.

nodes.name: compute_loc_changed
nodes.summary: Computes the lines-added/lines-deleted summary for the worktree against the recorded base sha by parsing `git diff --numstat`.

nodes.name: Decision
nodes.summary: Lifeguard verdict enum: Continue (allow the action) or Escalate (the loop has tripped a guardrail and must surface).

nodes.name: Lifeguard
nodes.summary: Stateful guardrail tracking per-action repeat counts (action_counts), the last canonical hash, consecutive parse failures, and the configured max_repeat / max_parse_failures thresholds.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start at the README to learn what loopr-v5 is: an agent orchestrator built around Plan decomposition, designed as a clean-break Rust workspace rewrite from v4. The README is intentionally short and points you at the canonical entry docs (vision, roadmap, CLAUDE.md) and at the build commands you will use throughout. The roadmap sits alongside as the living index of the ten incremental stages from scaffold-compiles (Stage 0) to the rust-version First Gate E2E (Stage 9), so you can see what is built, what is next, and where current work lands.

tour.title: The Architectural Front Door
tour.description: Read docs/vision.md next. It is the canonical statement of the v5 architecture: the compiler-style pipeline of typed stages, the per-crate ABI contracts, the target-repo .loopr/ layout, the observability strategy, and the AutoResearch story. The root CLAUDE.md complements it with the working rules that apply to every commit (seam tests at every crate boundary, no coexistence migrations, the crate as the unit of blast radius) and with the canonical crate map you will follow for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Workspace Shape and CI
tour.description: Before opening any Rust source, look at how the workspace itself is wired. Cargo.toml declares the workspace package metadata (single workspace.package.version inherited by every crate via version.workspace = true), the 13 member crates, and the shared dependency surface. The repo-root .otto.yml defines the full lint + check + test pipeline that runs as 'otto ci' at the workspace root and is scoped per-crate by an .otto.yml file inside each crate directory. Together these two files are the workspace-configuration layer that anchors everything that follows.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo workspaces let many crates share a single Cargo.lock, a single target/ directory, and inheritable [workspace.package] / [workspace.dependencies] tables. Each member crate's Cargo.toml then declares 'version.workspace = true' and 'serde.workspace = true' to inherit, so a single bump propagates everywhere and dependency versions stay aligned across crates.

tour.title: Application Binary Entry Point
tour.description: The loopr binary follows a strict 'thin main, thick lib' rule: main.rs only parses CLI args and delegates to lib::run, while lib.rs holds all real logic and dispatches Init / Plan / Plans / Works / Bundles / Ticks / Show / Daemon / Logs / Sessions subcommands across the daemon, plan, session, and logs modules. cli.rs is the clap-derive declaration of those subcommands. lib.rs is the highest-fan-in and highest-fan-out node in the workspace - it is the real hub of the binary and the thing the rest of crates/loopr/src/ branches out from.
tour.languageLesson: Rust binary crates can ship both src/main.rs and src/lib.rs side by side: main.rs becomes the executable, lib.rs becomes a library importable as the same crate name. The 'thin main, thick lib' convention puts all logic in lib.rs::run so it can be unit-tested without spawning a process, while main.rs stays a five-line wrapper around clap parsing.

tour.title: Daemon Lifecycle and State
tour.description: loopr runs as a long-lived background daemon. daemon.rs handles the process lifecycle - double-fork detachment, pid/version/process-id sentinels, signal handling, the accept-loop bootstrap, and a reverse-toposort drain on shutdown. daemon/context.rs defines DaemonContext, the shared per-daemon state that holds the typed store, the summary fanout, every agent JoinSet, the work/bundle scope maps, and the per-Plan operator_notifies / director chat sinks - this is the 'shared mutable world' the rest of the binary mutates through. daemon/startup.rs holds the crash recovery sweeps that reconcile on-disk state with what the daemon expects to find when it comes back up.

tour.title: Domain Records and Typed Storage
tour.description: Now drop into the Domain Core layer. The domain crate is pure, I/O-free typed core: it declares the Records (Plan, Work, Bundle, Tick, Note, Verdict, Role, Criteria, ID) and the FSM tables that drive valid transitions. domain/fsm.rs defines the state machines themselves, while every crate in the workspace re-exports its public types. The store crate is the typed anti-corruption layer over scottidler/taskstore - it wraps JSONL + SQLite + git-hooks underneath but presents a clean per-collection handle and update-sink API to callers. Together these two crates establish the vocabulary everything else speaks.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's newtype + trait pattern lets crates expose strongly typed wrappers around weaker primitives. Here, store wraps the more permissive scottidler/taskstore types in domain-specific Plan / Work / Bundle handles, so every read and write is checked at the type level and miswiring (e.g. saving a Work as a Bundle) is a compile error rather than a runtime bug.

tour.title: Daemon-Client IPC Wire Protocol
tour.description: The CLI subcommands from Step 4 do not run in the daemon process - they connect to it. The ipc crate defines the typed wire protocol: NDJSON envelopes with a MAX_LINE_BYTES (1 MiB) framing cap and a PROTOCOL_VERSION constant. ipc/envelope.rs holds the message variants (commands the client sends, responses + events the daemon emits); ipc/frame.rs holds the line-framing read/write primitives. The crate is deliberately transport-agnostic - it defines messages and framing only, with the actual UDS / TCP transport living over in the loopr binary's transport.rs.
tour.languageLesson: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) is a poor man's framing protocol: each message is one self-contained JSON object terminated by a newline. It gives you cheap streaming and trivial debugging (you can cat the socket) at the cost of a length cap - ipc fixes that at 1 MiB per line so a hostile or buggy sender cannot OOM the daemon.

tour.title: External Adapters: LLM, Context, and Tools
tour.description: These three crates form the External Adapters layer - everything that touches the world outside the domain core. llm exposes an LlmClient trait with an Anthropic backend, a MeteredLlmClient wrapper, a ScriptedLlm test stub, and a tool-schema bridge. context owns prompt assembly: handlebars templates + partials + token budgeting, plus role-specific input types (DirectorState, ResearchQuery, etc.) used by the decomposer and the per-role agent loops. tools defines the Tool trait, the bwrap-sandboxed builtins (read, write, edit, grep, ...), and the lane classifier that decides which tools an agent in a given role is allowed to call.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits with associated types let you define an abstract 'capability' interface (Tool, LlmClient) that concrete implementations (AnthropicClient, GrepTool) plug into. Because the trait is the contract, the decomposer and agents crates depend on the trait, not on a specific backend - so swapping Anthropic for a local model or a scripted test stub is a wiring change, not a refactor.

tour.title: Git Worktree Isolation
tour.description: Every Work runs in its own sibling git worktree so that an in-flight agent edit cannot contaminate another agent's branch or the integration branch. worktree/handle.rs exposes the Worktree handle type, worktree/ops.rs holds the create / cleanup / list operations, and lib.rs re-exports the free functions plus the WorktreeConfig and WorktreeError types. A registry tracks every active worktree on disk, and crash recovery (referenced by daemon/startup.rs in Step 5) reconciles the registry with what git actually has when the daemon restarts after a crash.
tour.languageLesson: git worktrees let one repository check out multiple branches into multiple sibling directories simultaneously, sharing the underlying .git object database. loopr uses one worktree per Work so agents can edit in parallel without lock contention, and the integrator (Step 10) merges those branches into a single per-Plan integration branch.

tour.title: Pipeline Stages: Decomposer, Agents, Integrator
tour.description: This is the heart of loopr - the compiler-style pipeline that turns a Goal into shipped Work. decomposer takes a Plan and produces a Work DAG (modules: cycles, decompose, prompt, tool, tree). agents runs per-role Ralph loops on each Work: implementer.rs writes code, reviewer.rs reviews it, and director.rs (with config, dispatch, lifeguard, scope) decides when to retry, escalate, or accept. integrator is non-LLM by design - it does merge-validate-publish with sequential no-ff git merges of accepted bundles, preflight checks, and a typed verdict. The three stages share the context crate from Step 8 for prompt assembly and the store/domain crates from Step 6 for typed state.

tour.title: Foundation: Telemetry and Derive Macros
tour.description: Finish at the Foundation layer - the zero-dependency primitives every other crate consumes. telemetry initialises the tracing subscriber, declares the span-prefix constants (stage., ralph., tool.) that show up throughout the codebase, owns the run-id propagation strategy, and provides the log-query and transcript helpers used by tests and the loopr logs subcommand. derive is the proc-macro crate that provides #[derive(Fsm)] (auto-generates validate_transition / validate_override / is_terminal from a state-machine table) and #[derive(Record)] - derives only, no fn-like or attribute macros, per the v5 working rules. Reading these last makes the tracing decorations and Fsm derives you saw throughout the earlier steps stop looking like magic.
tour.languageLesson: Rust proc macros run at compile time and operate on the syntax tree. #[derive(Fsm)] in loopr-derive reads the annotated enum + a transitions table and generates the validate_transition / validate_override / is_terminal functions, so the FSM tables in the domain crate stay declarative data instead of hand-written match arms - a single source of truth that the compiler enforces.
